source.title: SAFEPATH: Preventing Harmful Reasoning in Chain-of-Thought via Early Alignment
source.authors: Wonje Jeung; Sangyeon Yoon; Minsuk Kahng; Albert No

record.tranche_reason: Measures outcomes of a compliant-opening prefilling attack and evaluates an early safety-primer intervention under harmful prompts and jailbreaks. The method differs from the original studies’ fine-tuning and token-position analyses.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, harmful-example fine-tuning that induces compliance, benign fine-tuning that erodes safety, or safety localized in weights. Rows cover its prefilling-attack results and its trained Safety Primer safety/activation results. Other attack benchmarks, capability and reasoning scores, training time, and comparisons of alternative caution/refusal prefixes are not rows because they do not directly test these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study applies a compliant-opening prefill inside the reasoning block of DeepSeek-R1-distilled reasoning models, before and after several safety trainings (V4). It also reports whether an opening-only safety primer re-emerges later in reasoning and survives that prefill (V7, indirectly). This is a new setting (reasoning models, reasoning-block prefill) rather than the originals' chat-model method. It does not test fine-tuning attacks, per-token KL, or parameter localization.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that an 8-token Safety Primer trained only at the start of reasoning reduces harmful outputs (up to 90%) and jailbreak success (83.3% blocked in R-8B) while preserving reasoning, at far lower training cost. They present mid-reasoning primer reactivation under adversarial prompts as emergent and akin to Qi et al.'s deep alignment. They acknowledge PAIR ASR above 25%.
record.recipe_differences: This paper trains reasoning models to emit a safety-oriented primer, rather than testing harmful-example or benign-example fine-tuning effects on safety-trained chat models, or measuring per-token KL. It also reports a zero-shot primer variant.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by model, attack type, training method, and primer placement. Prefilling attack rates vary across methods; the paper reports lower harmfulness for prefix than suffix placement and varies the safety-data ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Training only the first 8 reasoning tokens to emit a safety primer cuts harmfulness and PAIR ASR in reasoning models. Harmfulness falls 49.2→10.4 and 36.2→7.7; PAIR ASR falls 95.0→26.3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An opening-position safety cue can produce broad safety gains in reasoning models.

fits_no_version.finding: In the zero-shot setting, a safety phrase placed at the start of reasoning lowers StrongReject harmfulness more than the same phrase appended at the end. The gap is 30.4 points for R-7B and 18.1 for R-8B (Figure 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early-position safety signals matter more than late ones in reasoning traces.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. StrongReject uses 60 sampled prompts and PAIR uses 80 samples. The claim of adaptive reactivation is supported by activation counts and qualitative examples, without a reported causal analysis of why it occurs. PAIR remains effective on more than 25% of tested samples for both SAFEPATH models.
record.rows_left_out: No other directly relevant results omitted. Excluded unrelated attack benchmarks (DAN, Trigger, Multilingual), general-capability and reasoning-accuracy results, training/inference times, and alternative CautionPath/RefusalPath comparisons; they do not directly test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning attacks are not run.
Benign fine-tuning erosion is not measured.
No per-token KL or position-wise comparison of aligned vs base models.
Adversarial suffixes (GCG) and decoding changes are untested. Only one reasoning-block prefill phrase is used, and no response-opening prefill.
No weight or rank localization analysis.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.

No comparison with Qi et al.'s deep-alignment augmentation or token-wise constrained objective. No fine-tuning-attack durability test. No prefill-depth sweep. No causal test that reactivation produces safety.

missing.what: Prefilling ASR for the TA, NPO and CB baselines on R-8B (31.3, 9.0, 51.7). Each is below that method's no-attack BeaverTails harmfulness (46.0, 31.1, 62.2), extending the V4 reversal pattern.
Per-method no-attack BeaverTails harmfulness should be recorded as the baseline for each prefill row.
Zero-shot primer placement result: prefix vs suffix on StrongReject for R-7B and R-8B.

record.verdict_notes: The reader compared prefill ASR across methods against base-model prefill ASR. For V4 the right comparison is each model's own no-attack harmfulness. On that comparison, reasoning-block prefill barely raises, or even lowers, harmfulness. That conclusion assumes the prefill and BeaverTails harmfulness numbers share the BeaverDam scorer, which C.2 implies but does not state. The base distilled models are described as weakly aligned, so they are weak tests of V4's safety-trained premise. SafePath itself is an opening-only intervention, so its link to V7 is indirect. The prefill phrase sits where SP's primer would go, but the paper does not show whether SP re-emits the primer after the prefill.

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful examples make safety-trained models comply with harmful requests.
Whether ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Adversarial suffixes and decoding changes; the paper tests a specific compliant-opening prefilling attack and a safety-phrase placement comparison.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
No direct comparison of safety depth across response positions or training objectives; no systematic test of whether reactivation is caused by the primer-training objective.
